title: Compile-Time vs Runtime Polymorphism
statement: Which mechanism demonstrates Runtime Polymorphism in object-oriented programming languages like Java or C++?

options.text: Method Overriding with Virtual Functions / Dynamic Dispatch
Method Overloading with different parameter counts

explanation: Method Overriding achieves runtime polymorphism via late binding (dynamic dispatch / vtable), resolving the method call at runtime based on the actual object type rather than the reference type.

title: Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)
statement: According to the Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP) in SOLID design:

options.text: Derived classes must be substitutable for their base classes without altering the correctness of the program
A class should have only one reason to change
High-level modules should depend on abstractions, not concretions
Clients should not be forced to depend on interfaces they do not use

explanation: LSP states that objects of a superclass should be replaceable with objects of its subclasses without breaking application behavior or violating preconditions/postconditions.
